Understanding Redeemable Deeds

What are Redeemable Deeds?

A redeemable deed is a type of tax deed that allows the original property owner a set period, called the redemption period, to reclaim their property after it has been sold at a tax auction. During this redemption period, the buyer holds the deed but doesn’t gain full ownership rights immediately. Instead, the original owner has the right to “redeem” the property by paying the back taxes owed plus a penalty. If the owner redeems within the allowed period, the investor receives the penalty as compensation. However, if the redemption period passes without repayment, the buyer then gains full ownership of the property.

Example of Potential Returns

Imagine you buy a tax deed for $1,000. If the original owner redeems the property within a year, you could earn a penalty of up to 25%, giving you $1,250 back. If they don’t redeem it, you get the property outright.

Process of Tax Deed Auctions in Collin County

In Collin County, properties are auctioned to recover unpaid taxes. These auctions happen on the first Tuesday of every month at the Collin County Courthouse. Here’s how it works:

Non-Homestead, Non-Agricultural, and Non-Mineral Rights Real Estate:

  • Redemption period: 6 months
  • Penalty: 25%

Homestead, Agricultural, or Mineral Rights Properties:

  • Redemption period: 2 years
  • Penalty: Up to 50%

Steps to Start Tax Deed Investing in Collin County

1. Research and Understand Local Laws

Knowing the legal framework is crucial. Each county has specific rules, so start by visiting the Collin County Website.

2. Visit the Local Treasurer’s Website

Check out the Collin County Sheriff’s Office for details on tax deed sales. They provide comprehensive information about upcoming sales and the auction process.

3. Check the Auction Site

Auctions are held at the Collin County Courthouse, 2100 Bloomdale Rd., McKinney, Texas, 75071. Make sure to visit the site to familiarize yourself with the location and process.

4. Read the Details About Tax Deeds

Understanding the sale schedule and parcel inquiry is vital. Thoroughly research the properties listed for auction to avoid any unforeseen issues.

5. Contact the County Office

For additional inquiries, contact the county office. They can provide valuable insights and answer specific questions you might have.
